newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK bank shares tumble after Halifax debut.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK bank shares tumble after Halifax debut.

text.p: Shares in leading UK bank stocks tumbled on Monday, as the long awaited market debut of the Halifax, Britain's biggest home loans provider, triggered a bout of profit-taking in the banks sector, dealers and analysts said.

The sell-off, which started last week, follows two months of sharp gains by the sector as professional investors feared they might miss out on the Halifax, which would have left their portfolio weightings light in the increasingly dominant bank sector.
Abbey National shares fell back 33p to 847-1/2p, Barclays Plc dropped 52p to 1135p while Lloyds TSB Group declined 30p to 584p.

Dealers said the sudden reversal in bank stocks had been on the cards as Halifax made its long-awaited market debut. "The sector has shown a strong performance and there are now those who think it is time to take profits," said Nick Collier, analyst at Morgan Stanley.
"The shares have had a huge run," said Phil Pickard, analyst at HSBC James Capel. "I suspect there has been selling of some banking shares to pay for Halifax stock," said another analyst.
In addition renewed fears of a rise in interest rates also added pressure to bank shares.
Economists said a raft of economic data showing Britain's manufacturers perking up while consumer demand remains robust raised the likelihood of an interest rate rise this week.
Higher interest rates act to discourage borrowing, thereby affecting the banks' main business, as well as tending to narrow the margin between lending and borrowing rates.
Some brokers have recently turned more cautious on the financial services sector and reduced their weightings.
Strategists at Goldman Sachs cut their recommended weighting on the sector on Friday to "underweight" from "neutral."

Other analysts said the spread of 710p to 815p per share achieved at the Halifax auction this morning of around 570 million shares on behalf of the formerly mutually-owned society's savers and borrowers, showed that some institutions were holding too many at too high a price in the short term.
Halifax shares opened their trading at 774-1/2p before falling back to close at 735-1/2p.
